entries.symptom: Phone completely dead, no charging indicator
entries.root_cause: PMIC MT6357 dead due to water damage corrosion on power rail capacitors
entries.fix_description: Replaced PMIC MT6357 and cleaned corrosion. Replaced 3 shorted capacitors near PMIC.
repair_steps: 1. Removed motherboard and cleaned with ultrasonic cleaner
2. Found corrosion around PMIC area (C3201, C3205, C3208 shorted)
3. Replaced shorted capacitors (0201 100nF)
4. Reballed and replaced PMIC MT6357
5. Tested all power rails — all normal
6. Phone boots and charges normally

entries.symptom: WiFi and Bluetooth both not working
entries.root_cause: WCN3988 combo IC had dry solder joints from drop damage
entries.fix_description: Reballed WCN3988 combo IC. WiFi and Bluetooth restored.
repair_steps: 1. Confirmed both WiFi and BT dead (MAC addresses 00:00:00:00:00:00)
2. Checked combo IC power supply — voltages OK
3. Removed and reballed WCN3988 with fresh solder
4. Reflowed back onto board
5. WiFi and BT both working, MAC addresses restored

entries.symptom: Phone boot loops, stuck at Samsung logo
entries.root_cause: eMMC NAND pages corrupted, preloader partition damaged
entries.fix_description: Reflashed preloader and full firmware via ODIN. eMMC health was 70%, still usable.
repair_steps: 1. Entered download mode (Vol Down + Power)
2. Connected to ODIN, detected device
3. Flashed stock firmware (BL + AP + CP + CSC)
4. First boot took 5 minutes (optimization)
5. Checked eMMC health — 70% life remaining
6. Advised customer to back up data and consider upgrade

entries.symptom: No display, phone vibrates and makes sounds
entries.root_cause: Display FPC connector pin damaged (pin 23 bent), causing no display signal
entries.fix_description: Carefully straightened bent pin 23 on FPC connector. Display works.
repair_steps: 1. Phone vibrates on power button — motherboard alive
2. Connected known-good display — still no display
3. Inspected FPC connector under microscope
4. Found pin 23 (MIPI data lane) bent inward
5. Carefully straightened pin with tweezers under microscope
6. Reconnected display — works perfectly

entries.symptom: Phone overheating near camera area, battery draining fast
entries.root_cause: Decoupling capacitor C4115 (near camera power rail) shorted internally
entries.fix_description: Located hot spot using thermal camera, found shorted capacitor C4115, removed it.
repair_steps: 1. Thermal camera showed hot spot near camera area (65°C)
2. Measured current draw: 850mA at idle (should be 200mA)
3. Isolated area — hot spot was capacitor C4115
4. Removed C4115 (0201 size)
5. Current draw dropped to 180mA, temperature normalized
6. Phone works fine without C4115 (decoupling cap, non-critical)

entries.symptom: No IMEI, no network signal, baseband unknown
entries.root_cause: Modem firmware corrupted after failed OTA update
entries.fix_description: Reflashed modem partition (CP) separately via ODIN. IMEI restored.
repair_steps: 1. Confirmed baseband version = 'unknown' in About Phone
2. IMEI showed null when dialing *#06#
3. Entered download mode and connected to ODIN
4. Flashed only CP (modem) partition from stock firmware
5. Rebooted — baseband version appeared
6. IMEI restored, network signal working

entries.symptom: No charging, USB not detected by PC
entries.root_cause: USB-C port sub-board flex cable torn (internal break, not visible externally)
entries.fix_description: Replaced USB sub-board/charging flex. Phone charges and connects to PC.
repair_steps: 1. Tested with multiple cables — no charging, no USB detection
2. Checked charging IC on motherboard — voltages normal when powered by bench supply
3. Tested USB port continuity — data lines open circuit
4. Replaced USB sub-board / charging flex assembly
5. Charging and USB data both working

entries.symptom: Random reboots, especially when using camera
entries.root_cause: RAM BGA cold solder joints from drop damage, causing intermittent connection loss
entries.fix_description: Reballed RAM (PoP package). Random reboots stopped.
repair_steps: 1. Checked kernel logs — multiple 'machine check' and 'memory errors'
2. Ran memtest via JTAG — intermittent failures at 0x80000000-0x9FFFFFFF
3. Removed CPU+RAM PoP package
4. Found cracked solder balls on RAM BGA
5. Reballed RAM with fresh solder balls (0.25mm LPDDR4X stencil)
6. Reassembled — no more random reboots after 48hr test

entries.symptom: Earpiece speaker not working, loudspeaker OK
entries.root_cause: Earpiece speaker coil open circuit (water damage)
entries.fix_description: Replaced earpiece speaker module. Audio calls working.
repair_steps: 1. Tested loudspeaker — OK
2. Tested earpiece during call — no sound
3. Measured earpiece resistance — open circuit (should be 28-32 ohms)
4. Found water damage residue on earpiece contacts
5. Replaced earpiece speaker module
6. Measured new earpiece — 30 ohms, sounds clear

entries.symptom: Fingerprint sensor not responding
entries.root_cause: Fingerprint flex cable connector not fully seated after screen replacement
entries.fix_description: Reseated fingerprint flex cable connector. Sensor working.
repair_steps: 1. Fingerprint option not showing in settings
2. Opened phone — found fingerprint flex partially disconnected
3. Cleaned connector with IPA
4. Properly seated and locked flex cable connector
5. Fingerprint sensor detected, enrollment working

entries.symptom: Phone completely dead, no response to charger or button press
entries.root_cause: PMIC S2MPS21 failed after voltage spike from non-OEM charger, VPH_PWR rail shorted to ground
entries.fix_description: Replaced PMIC S2MPS21. Removed shorted capacitor C5012 on VPH_PWR rail.
repair_steps: 1. No current draw on ammeter when connected to bench supply at 4.2V
2. Checked VPH_PWR rail — shorted to ground (0.02 ohms)
3. Injected voltage on VPH_PWR — capacitor C5012 got hot
4. Removed C5012 — short cleared
5. Replaced PMIC S2MPS21 (reballed donor IC)
6. Phone boots, all rails measured normal

entries.symptom: Phone dead, slight current draw (20mA) but no boot
entries.root_cause: MT6365 PMIC not generating VSRAM_PROC rail due to internal die failure
entries.fix_description: Replaced PMIC MT6365. All power rails restored, phone boots normally.
repair_steps: 1. Bench supply shows 20mA draw at 4.2V — PMIC partially alive
2. Checked VSRAM_PROC rail — 0V (should be 0.8V)
3. Other rails (VCORE, VDRAM) also missing
4. Removed and replaced PMIC MT6365
5. All rails came up correctly after replacement
6. Phone boots to Android, tested 24hr — stable

entries.symptom: Phone dead after drop, no charging LED
entries.root_cause: PMIC MT6358 cracked BGA balls from drop impact, intermittent power rail failures
entries.fix_description: Reballed PMIC MT6358 with fresh solder. Phone powers on and boots.
repair_steps: 1. No current draw on bench supply — completely dead
2. Pressed on PMIC area with finger — phone drew 50mA briefly
3. Confirmed PMIC BGA fracture (drop damage indicator)
4. Removed PMIC MT6358 — visible cracked balls on pads 12-18
5. Reballed with 0.2mm leaded solder balls
6. Reflowed back — phone boots, stress tested by tapping board

entries.symptom: Phone completely dead, used third-party charger
entries.root_cause: PM6125 PMIC burned out from overvoltage on VBUS line (charger supplied 12V on 5V pin)
entries.fix_description: Replaced PM6125 PMIC and burned TVS diode D4001. Phone restored.
repair_steps: 1. No response on bench supply, smelled burned component
2. Visual inspection found burned TVS diode D4001 near USB port
3. Replaced D4001, still dead — PMIC damaged too
4. Replaced PM6125 PMIC from donor board
5. All power rails restored
6. Phone boots and charges with OEM charger

entries.symptom: Phone not charging, shows charging icon but battery percentage stays same
entries.root_cause: Charging IC SM5714 not switching to charge mode, BATFET stuck open
entries.fix_description: Replaced charging IC SM5714. Phone charges normally at 25W.
repair_steps: 1. Phone shows charging animation but battery stays at same percentage
2. Measured VBUS on USB port — 9V present (PD negotiation OK)
3. Measured battery voltage at BATFET output — same as before plugging in
4. SM5714 BATFET not closing — IC faulty
5. Replaced SM5714 charging IC
6. Battery charging at 25W, charges 0-100% in 70 minutes

entries.symptom: Not charging, charging IC area hot
entries.root_cause: MAX77705 charger IC shorted internally, causing excessive heat and no charge current
entries.fix_description: Replaced MAX77705 charging/PMIC IC. Charging restored at 25W.
repair_steps: 1. Phone gets hot near battery connector area when plugged in
2. Thermal camera pinpointed MAX77705 at 85°C
3. Measured charge current — 0mA to battery despite VBUS present
4. Removed MAX77705 — short on BATT_ID pin cleared
5. Replaced MAX77705 from donor S22 board
6. Charges at 25W, temperature normal (38°C during charge)

entries.symptom: Boot loop, stuck at Mi logo, vibrates repeatedly
entries.root_cause: eMMC NAND blocks worn out (0% health), cannot read system partition
entries.fix_description: Replaced eMMC IC with new KLMBG2JETD-B041 (32GB). Flashed full firmware via UFi box.
repair_steps: 1. Phone stuck at Mi logo, vibrate-reboot loop every 10 seconds
2. Connected via EDL mode — eMMC health shows 0%
3. Multiple bad blocks reported in system and userdata partitions
4. Removed old eMMC with hot air at 340°C
5. Soldered new KLMBG2JETD-B041 eMMC
6. Programmed via UFi box — full firmware written, phone boots clean

entries.symptom: Boot loop after OTA update, stuck at Oppo logo
entries.root_cause: OTA update corrupted super partition, dm-verity check failing at boot
entries.fix_description: Flashed full firmware via MSMDownloadTool in EDL mode. Phone boots normally.
repair_steps: 1. Phone stuck at Oppo logo, reboots every 15 seconds
2. Could not enter recovery mode — also boot loops
3. Forced EDL mode (test point method on Oppo A17)
4. Connected MSMDownloadTool, flashed full OFP firmware package
5. Phone booted clean — factory reset state
6. Verified OTA updates work on fresh install

entries.symptom: Battery drains from 100% to 0% in 3 hours with screen off
entries.root_cause: Capacitor C7803 on VDD_MODEM rail partially shorted, drawing 120mA constant leakage
entries.fix_description: Removed shorted capacitor C7803. Standby current dropped from 150mA to 8mA.
repair_steps: 1. Measured standby current — 150mA with screen off (should be under 15mA)
2. Disconnected display, cameras, sub-board — still 140mA on motherboard alone
3. Thermal camera showed warm spot on C7803 near modem area
4. Measured C7803 — 35 ohms (should be open or >1K ohms)
5. Removed C7803 — standby current dropped to 8mA
6. Battery life back to normal (2 days standby)

entries.symptom: Battery drains fast, phone warm even when idle
entries.root_cause: Water damage caused partial short on camera power rail VREG_L6, 90mA leakage through corroded via
entries.fix_description: Cleaned corroded via near camera connector with IPA and resoldered ground pad.
repair_steps: 1. Standby current 95mA — abnormally high
2. Removed camera module — current dropped to 12mA
3. Inspected camera connector area — greenish corrosion on via hole
4. Cleaned with IPA and fiberglass pen
5. Resoldered exposed ground pad with fresh solder
6. Reconnected camera — standby current 10mA, camera works

entries.symptom: Green vertical line on AMOLED display, appeared suddenly
entries.root_cause: AMOLED panel internal COF (Chip on Film) driver IC partial failure, column driver shorted
entries.fix_description: Display panel replacement — no board-level fix for internal AMOLED driver failure.
repair_steps: 1. Green line visible from boot — not software related
2. Line persists in recovery mode and download mode
3. Tested with known-good display — no green line (confirms panel fault)
4. Replaced AMOLED display assembly (screen + digitizer + frame)
5. New display clean, no lines, touch working
6. Calibrated display via service mode (*#0*#)

entries.symptom: Multiple green and pink lines on display after minor drop
entries.root_cause: AMOLED flex cable partially cracked at bend point from drop, intermittent MIPI data lane connection
entries.fix_description: Replaced AMOLED display assembly. Lines caused by cracked flex, not repairable.
repair_steps: 1. Multiple colored lines appeared after drop (no screen crack visible)
2. Lines change pattern when pressing on bottom of screen (flex area)
3. Flex cable has internal micro-fracture at bend — not visible externally
4. Replaced full AMOLED assembly
5. Display perfect, tested touch grid — all zones responsive

entries.symptom: No display output, backlight works (screen lights up white/dim)
entries.root_cause: ESD damage on MIPI DSI data lane — filter capacitor C1205 shorted on DSI_D0 line
entries.fix_description: Removed shorted ESD filter capacitor C1205 on MIPI DSI data lane. Display restored.
repair_steps: 1. Backlight comes on but no image — MIPI signal issue
2. Tested with known-good display — same symptom (motherboard fault)
3. Checked MIPI DSI lines with oscilloscope — DSI_D0 stuck low
4. Traced DSI_D0 line — ESD filter cap C1205 shorted to ground
5. Removed C1205 (0201 size) — display signal restored
6. Display works perfectly, touch OK

entries.symptom: Touch not working after third-party screen replacement
entries.root_cause: Aftermarket display has incompatible touch controller firmware, needs re-initialization via I2C
entries.fix_description: Flashed correct touch firmware for aftermarket panel via I2C programmer. Touch restored.
repair_steps: 1. Display shows image perfectly but zero touch response
2. Checked touch connector — seated properly
3. Tested original broken display — touch works on uncracked areas
4. Aftermarket panel uses different touch IC revision
5. Connected I2C programmer to touch IC test pads
6. Flashed matching touch firmware — touch fully functional

entries.symptom: Ghost touch — screen registers random touches without being touched
entries.root_cause: Display ground connection broken at flex cable, digitizer floating causing capacitive noise
entries.fix_description: Repaired display ground connection with jumper wire from flex ground pad to board ground.
repair_steps: 1. Phone randomly opens apps, types characters — classic ghost touch
2. Tested in safe mode — still happens (rules out software)
3. Disconnected and reconnected display — ghost touch persists
4. Measured ground continuity on display flex — open circuit on GND pin 2
5. Soldered 0.1mm jumper wire from flex GND pad to nearest board ground
6. Ghost touch completely resolved, digitizer stable

entries.symptom: Display flickers and goes black intermittently
entries.root_cause: BTB (Board-to-Board) display connector loose retention clip broken from previous repair
entries.fix_description: Replaced BTB connector on motherboard. Display connection stable.
repair_steps: 1. Display randomly goes black for 1-2 seconds then comes back
2. Tapping phone or tilting triggers the flicker
3. Opened phone — BTB connector retention clip broken on one side
4. Display flex not held firmly in socket
5. Desoldered old BTB connector, soldered new one
6. Display stable, no flicker during 48hr vibration test

entries.symptom: Touch dead in bottom third of screen, rest works fine
entries.root_cause: Touch controller Goodix GT9916 partial channel failure, TX lines 28-39 not driven
entries.fix_description: Replaced Goodix GT9916 touch IC on display flex. Full touch restored.
repair_steps: 1. Touch test app shows bottom 1/3 of screen has no touch response
2. Ruled out display flex damage — continuity OK on all pins
3. Scoped TX drive lines on touch IC — lines 28-39 dead (0V, no drive signal)
4. Touch IC GT9916 partial die failure
5. Replaced GT9916 on display flex PCB (hot air, fine pitch)
6. All touch zones responsive, tested with touch grid app

entries.symptom: WiFi turns on but cannot find any networks, Bluetooth works fine
entries.root_cause: WCN6856 WiFi antenna switch path damaged, BT antenna path OK (separate RF paths)
entries.fix_description: Replaced RF filter FL3501 on WiFi antenna path. WiFi scanning and connecting normally.
repair_steps: 1. WiFi toggle works but 'Scanning...' never finds networks
2. Bluetooth scans and pairs fine — combo IC partially alive
3. Checked WiFi antenna continuity — OK
4. Measured RF filter FL3501 on WiFi path — open circuit
5. Replaced FL3501 with matching SAW filter
6. WiFi finds networks, connects, speed test 120Mbps

entries.symptom: WiFi and Bluetooth both dead, MAC address shows 00:00:00:00:00:00
entries.root_cause: WCN6750 combo IC dead from ESD — VDDO supply rail shorted internally
entries.fix_description: Replaced WCN6750 combo IC. WiFi and BT fully restored.
repair_steps: 1. WiFi toggle grayed out, BT also dead
2. MAC addresses all zeros — IC not initializing
3. Checked WCN6750 supply rails — VDDO shorted (0.5 ohms to ground)
4. Removed WCN6750 — short cleared
5. Replaced with new WCN6750
6. WiFi and BT both working, MAC addresses restored

entries.symptom: WiFi connects but disconnects every 30 seconds, Bluetooth stutters
entries.root_cause: MT6631 combo IC crystal oscillator (26MHz) drifted out of spec from heat damage, causing timing errors
entries.fix_description: Replaced 26MHz crystal Y3501 near MT6631. WiFi and BT stable.
repair_steps: 1. WiFi connects then drops — 'authentication error' in logs
2. BT audio stutters every few seconds
3. Both symptoms point to clock/timing issue on combo IC
4. Measured 26MHz crystal Y3501 — frequency drifted to 25.997MHz (out of +/-10ppm spec)
5. Replaced Y3501 crystal oscillator
6. WiFi stays connected, BT audio smooth, tested 4hrs

entries.symptom: No network signal, 'Baseband unknown', IMEI present
entries.root_cause: Shannon 5300 RF transceiver cold solder joints from drop, modem initializes but RF path dead
entries.fix_description: Reballed Shannon 5300 RF transceiver. Network signal restored on all bands.
repair_steps: 1. IMEI shows via *#06# — modem alive, but baseband says 'unknown'
2. No signal bars on any carrier SIM
3. Service mode shows RF TX/RX power at -999dBm (no RF activity)
4. Reballed Shannon 5300 RF transceiver IC
5. Reflowed back — signal bars appeared immediately
6. Tested calls, data, SMS on both SIM slots — all working

entries.symptom: SIM 1 not detected, SIM 2 works fine
entries.root_cause: SIM1 reader IC contact pin corroded from moisture, SIMCLK line open circuit
entries.fix_description: Replaced SIM1 card reader. Both SIM slots functional.
repair_steps: 1. SIM1 shows 'No SIM detected' with known-good SIM
2. Same SIM works in SIM2 slot
3. Inspected SIM1 reader under microscope — pin 3 (SIMCLK) corroded
4. Cleaned with IPA — corrosion too deep, pin pad lifted
5. Replaced entire SIM1 card reader connector
6. Both SIM slots detect and register on network
parts_used: SIM card reader connector (6-pin push-push type)

entries.symptom: GPS not working, location stuck or jumps wildly
entries.root_cause: GPS LNA IC damaged from ESD through antenna contact, no GPS signal amplification
entries.fix_description: Replaced GPS LNA IC. GPS locks within 5 seconds, accuracy within 3 meters.
repair_steps: 1. GPS test app shows 0 satellites found (should see 10-15)
2. WiFi-based location works — confirms GPS hardware fault
3. Checked GPS antenna — continuity OK
4. Measured GPS LNA output — no gain (input = output, should be +15dB)
5. Replaced GPS LNA IC (SOT-363 package)
6. GPS now finds 12 satellites, locks in 5 seconds, 3m accuracy

entries.symptom: No SIM detected on both slots after water exposure
entries.root_cause: SIM voltage regulator VSIM shorted from water damage, both SIM slots share same VSIM rail
entries.fix_description: Replaced VSIM regulator capacitor C8501 and cleaned corroded traces. Both SIMs detected.
repair_steps: 1. Both SIM slots show 'No SIM' — inserted known-good SIMs
2. Water damage indicators triggered
3. Measured VSIM rail — 0V (should be 1.8V or 3.0V)
4. Found capacitor C8501 on VSIM rail shorted from corrosion
5. Removed C8501, cleaned traces, replaced with new 100nF cap
6. VSIM rail reads 1.8V, both SIMs detected and registered

entries.symptom: No sound from loudspeaker and earpiece, vibration works
entries.root_cause: WCD9370 audio codec IC dead from water damage, all audio output paths non-functional
entries.fix_description: Replaced WCD9370 audio codec IC. All audio outputs restored.
repair_steps: 1. No sound from speaker, earpiece, or headphone jack
2. Vibration motor works — not a complete I2S bus failure
3. Audio codec WCD9370 supply rail VDD_A present (1.8V OK)
4. I2S clock present at codec input but no output on SPK_OUT pins
5. Replaced WCD9370 — all audio paths working
6. Tested loudspeaker, earpiece, headphone jack, mic — all OK

entries.symptom: Microphone not working during calls, works on voice recorder
entries.fault_component: Primary Mic Trace / Mic Bias Resistor
entries.root_cause: Mic bias resistor R4201 (2.2K) open circuit, primary mic gets no DC bias voltage
entries.fix_description: Replaced mic bias resistor R4201. Primary mic works in calls and all apps.
repair_steps: 1. Caller cannot hear user during voice calls
2. Voice recorder works — uses secondary/noise cancellation mic
3. Primary mic on sub-board — physically OK, membrane intact
4. Measured mic bias voltage at motherboard connector — 0V (should be 2.7V)
5. Traced bias circuit — R4201 (2.2K ohm) open circuit
6. Replaced R4201 — mic bias 2.7V, calls clear both ways

entries.symptom: No sound during calls — earpiece and loudspeaker both silent in calls only
entries.root_cause: Audio amplifier IC AW87319 I2C communication failure, amp not enabled during call audio routing
entries.fix_description: Reballed AW87319 audio amplifier. Call audio restored on earpiece and speaker.
repair_steps: 1. No sound during calls on earpiece or speaker
2. Media audio plays fine (YouTube, music) — different audio path
3. Call audio routes through AW87319 amp — media bypasses it
4. Checked I2C lines to AW87319 — SDA line intermittent
5. Reballed AW87319 — I2C communication stable
6. Call audio works on both earpiece and loudspeaker modes

entries.symptom: Loudspeaker distorted at any volume, earpiece fine
entries.root_cause: Loudspeaker voice coil partially detached from diaphragm (physical wear/drop damage)
entries.fix_description: Replaced loudspeaker module. Sound clear at all volumes.
repair_steps: 1. Loudspeaker buzzes and distorts at all volume levels
2. Earpiece sounds clear — codec and amp OK
3. Measured loudspeaker impedance — 5 ohms (should be 8 ohms) indicating coil damage
4. Replaced loudspeaker module
5. New speaker measures 8 ohms, sounds clean at full volume
6. Tested music, ringtone, speakerphone call — all clear

entries.symptom: Recording audio has loud buzzing noise, calls also have static
entries.root_cause: Mic bias decoupling capacitor C4305 cracked, injecting power supply noise into mic signal
entries.fix_description: Replaced cracked mic bias capacitor C4305. Audio recording clean.
repair_steps: 1. Voice recordings have constant 50Hz buzz/hum
2. Call recipients hear static and buzzing
3. Both primary and secondary mic affected — common bias circuit
4. Scoped mic bias line — 100mV ripple (should be <1mV)
5. Found cracked capacitor C4305 (1uF) on mic bias filter
6. Replaced C4305 — ripple dropped to 0.2mV, recordings clean

entries.symptom: Rear camera shows 'Camera failed' error, front camera works
entries.root_cause: Camera LDO regulator U3501 not outputting VCAM_AF voltage (2.8V), autofocus power missing kills camera init
entries.fix_description: Replaced camera LDO regulator U3501. Rear camera opens and focuses normally.
repair_steps: 1. Rear camera shows 'Camera failed' immediately on open
2. Front camera works fine — not a software issue
3. Tested with known-good rear camera module — same error
4. Checked camera power rails — VCAM_IO (1.8V) OK, VCAM_AF (2.8V) missing
5. LDO U3501 output 0V — input present, IC dead
6. Replaced U3501 — VCAM_AF 2.8V, rear camera works

entries.symptom: Camera takes blurry photos, OIS makes clicking noise
entries.root_cause: OIS voice coil actuator spring broken from drop, lens element stuck off-center
entries.fix_description: Replaced main camera module (OIS actuator not separately serviceable). Photos sharp.
repair_steps: 1. Photos blurry even in good light, video has visible shake
2. Audible clicking/rattling from camera when phone tilted
3. OIS test in engineering mode shows actuator hitting limit stops
4. OIS VCM spring damaged — lens offset 0.3mm from center
5. Replaced entire main camera module (200MP, includes OIS actuator)
6. Photos sharp, OIS smooth and silent, video stabilization working

entries.symptom: Front camera shows black screen, rear camera works
entries.root_cause: Front camera flex cable torn during screen replacement, MIPI data lines broken
entries.fix_description: Replaced front camera module with new flex cable. Front camera functional.
repair_steps: 1. Front camera opens but shows solid black screen
2. Rear cameras all work — main app and camera IC OK
3. Phone had screen replaced recently (aftermarket repair)
4. Inspected front camera flex — small tear near connector (occurred during screen removal)
5. Replaced front camera module
6. Front camera preview and capture working, tested selfie and video call

entries.symptom: All cameras show 'Cannot connect to camera' error
entries.root_cause: Camera PMIC Fan53870 failed, no camera power rails generated (VCAM_IO, VCAM_A, VCAM_D all dead)
entries.fix_description: Replaced camera PMIC Fan53870. All three cameras functional.
repair_steps: 1. All cameras (main, ultra-wide, front) show connection error
2. Camera power rails: VCAM_IO 0V, VCAM_A 0V, VCAM_D 0V (all dead)
3. All camera power rails sourced from Fan53870 camera PMIC
4. Fan53870 input supply present (3.8V) but no outputs — IC dead
5. Replaced Fan53870 camera PMIC
6. All camera rails restored, all three cameras working

entries.symptom: Camera app crashes immediately, 'Camera failed' popup
entries.root_cause: Main camera BTB connector oxidized from humidity, intermittent I2C communication failure
entries.fix_description: Cleaned camera BTB connector contacts with IPA and contact cleaner. Camera stable.
repair_steps: 1. Camera app crashes on launch — 'Camera failed'
2. Sometimes works after reboot, then crashes again (intermittent)
3. Opened phone — camera BTB connector contacts have dull oxidation
4. Cleaned both connector and camera module contacts with IPA
5. Applied contact cleaner on BTB pins
6. Camera stable after 50+ open/close cycles, no crashes

entries.symptom: Slow charging — charges at 5W instead of 67W
entries.root_cause: SC8571 charge pump IC not switching, PD negotiation falls back to 5V/1A baseline
entries.fix_description: Replaced charge pump IC SC8571. 67W turbo charging restored.
repair_steps: 1. Phone charges but takes 5+ hours (should be 45 minutes at 67W)
2. Ampere app shows 5V/0.9A — no fast charge negotiation
3. Tested with OEM 67W charger and cable — same result
4. Checked charge pump SC8571 — VIN present but no switching activity
5. Replaced SC8571 charge pump IC
6. Phone now draws 11V/6A (67W), charges 0-100% in 45 minutes

entries.symptom: USB not detected by any PC, charging works fine
entries.root_cause: USB data mux switch IC stuck routing to UART debug instead of USB data lines
entries.fix_description: Replaced USB mux switch IC. USB data connection restored.
repair_steps: 1. Phone charges normally but PC shows 'USB device not recognized'
2. Tried multiple cables and PCs — same result
3. USB debug option enabled but phone never appears in ADB
4. USB mux switch IC stuck — routing D+/D- to UART instead of USB
5. Replaced USB mux switch IC (WLCSP package)
6. Phone appears in ADB, file transfer works, MTP functional

entries.symptom: 'Moisture detected' warning, USB port is dry
entries.root_cause: CC pin pull-down resistor R5002 (5.1K) drifted to 800 ohms from corrosion, triggering false moisture detection
entries.fix_description: Replaced corroded CC pin resistor R5002. Moisture warning cleared, charging works.
repair_steps: 1. Phone shows 'Moisture detected' but USB port completely dry
2. Cleaned USB port with IPA — warning persists
3. Cleared USB settings and cache — warning persists
4. Measured CC pin resistance — 800 ohms (should be 5.1K ohms)
5. R5002 corroded — replaced with new 5.1K 0201 resistor
6. Moisture warning gone, phone charges and connects normally

entries.symptom: Phone shows charging but current is negative — battery drains while plugged in
entries.root_cause: SMB1394 charging IC BATFET leaking in reverse — battery discharges through IC even with charger connected
entries.fix_description: Replaced SMB1394 charging IC. Charging current positive, battery charges normally.
repair_steps: 1. Phone shows charging icon but battery percentage drops slowly
2. Measured battery current — -200mA while 'charging' (negative = discharging)
3. VBUS present (9V from PD), but BATFET conducting in reverse
4. SMB1394 BATFET internal MOSFET has gate-drain short
5. Replaced SMB1394 IC
6. Charging current +3A at 9V, charges 0-100% normally

entries.symptom: Phone dead, no current draw, known PM8150 board
entries.root_cause: PM8550 PMIC VPH_PWR input FET burned from surge, zero current draw at any voltage
entries.fix_description: Replaced PM8550 PMIC. Phone boots and all functions working.
repair_steps: 1. Bench supply at 4.2V — 0mA draw, completely dead
2. Checked VPH_PWR — not shorted but PMIC not drawing any current
3. Applied voltage directly to PMIC VPH_PWR pin — still 0mA
4. PM8550 input protection FET open (burned open, not shorted)
5. Replaced PM8550 PMIC from donor S23 board
6. Phone draws normal boot current (250mA->1.2A), boots to Android

entries.symptom: Phone charges only when cable held at certain angle
entries.root_cause: USB-C port center tongue bent and VBUS contact pins worn from repeated insertion/removal
entries.fix_description: Replaced USB-C port on sub-board. Charges reliably with any cable.
repair_steps: 1. Charging only works with cable at specific angle — loose connection
2. Inspected USB port under microscope — center tongue bent slightly
3. VBUS contact pins (A4, B9) worn down, intermittent contact
4. Replaced USB-C port connector on sub-board (hot air + solder)
5. New port snaps cable firmly, VBUS solid connection
6. Charges at rated speed with any USB-C cable

entries.symptom: Green line appeared on AMOLED after phone got warm in sun
entries.root_cause: AMOLED panel COF bond wire degraded from thermal cycling, single column driver line failed
entries.fix_description: Display panel replacement required. COF bond is not field-repairable.
repair_steps: 1. Single bright green vertical line appeared after extended sun exposure
2. Line visible at all times including boot logo and recovery
3. Tested with known-good display — no line (panel fault confirmed)
4. COF bond area shows no visible damage but column driver line dead
5. Replaced AMOLED display assembly
6. New display clean, tested at various brightness levels — no artifacts

entries.symptom: Phone dead after water splash, short circuit on main board
entries.root_cause: Water ingress caused corrosion shorts on VDD_CX rail — capacitors C1102, C1105, C1108 all shorted
entries.fix_description: Ultrasonically cleaned board, replaced 3 shorted caps on VDD_CX rail. Phone restored.
repair_steps: 1. Phone completely dead, 1.8A short circuit on bench supply at 4.2V
2. Ultrasonic cleaning revealed corrosion on VDD_CX rail area
3. Injected 1V on VDD_CX — thermal camera showed C1102, C1105, C1108 all hot
4. Removed all three caps — short cleared (rail reads >10K ohms)
5. Replaced all three with new 0201 100nF capacitors
6. Phone boots, VDD_CX measures 0.75V, all functions tested OK
